newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB pushed up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB pushed up on short-covering.

text.p: Shares in Lloyds TSB Group Plc moved ahead to a fresh record high on Monday as the market sought to cover short positions, dealers said.
Lloyds TSB shares were up seven pence, or 1.26 percent, to 564p by 1150 GMT in volume of 3.2 million while the FTSE-100 index was 7.5 points, or 0.17 percent, higher at 4,377.2.
The stock touched a high at 567p, setting a fresh record high for the third consecutive session.
"The whole (banking) sector is quite buoyant at the moment," said a market-maker at a British firm.
The Alliance & Leicester floated last week and is due to be joined by the Halifax Building Society in early June, then the Woolwich Building Society later in the summer.
Some 27 percent of Alliance shares were put up for auction by the society's member's prior to flotation, a level which has ensured good institutional demand for the stock in the aftermath.
Alliance members who sold at those auctions received 533p a share, against the 540p minimum at which the stock has traded on the open market.

As a result, retail stockbrokers have since been recommending beneficiaries of the Halifax flotation should hold their shares, hoping for the price to be squeezed higher by institutions desperate to balance their weightings.
Around 7.6 million people will receive free Halifax shares when it is floated.
Other bank stocks 0#.FTBK also moved ahead this morning, led by Barclays, up 8.5p at 1095p.
